# Third-party notices

Margo Engine's own code is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (`LICENSE` and `NOTICE`; every tarball ships both). This file lists everything else that
reaches users: npm packages our published packages depend on, third-party code shipped inside our tarballs, and the
assets the site and examples use. It covers all 100 published packages (98 in `packages/`
plus `create-margo` and `margo-convert`). `node scripts/supply-chain.mjs --check` (in `npm run verify`, through
`tests/supply-chain.test.js`) fails when this file is stale, a dependency has no stated reason, a licence is outside
the allowed list, or a runtime dependency has an install script, a deprecation or a non-registry source.

## Runtime npm dependencies of published packages (direct and transitive)

90 of 100 packages have no third-party runtime dependency at all (internal `@margoengine/*` ranges only).
Versions are the ones in `package-lock.json`; users get whatever their own lockfile resolves inside our ranges.

| Package | Version (lock) | Licence | Kind | Used by | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@dimforge/rapier2d-compat` | 0.21.0 | Apache-2.0 | optional peer | @margoengine/physics2d, margoengine | Rapier 2D rigid-body solver; optional, the app installs and initializes it |
| `@dimforge/rapier3d-compat` | 0.21.0 | Apache-2.0 | optional peer | @margoengine/physics, margoengine | Rapier rigid-body solver; optional, the app installs and initializes it |
| `react` | 19.3.0 | MIT | optional peer | @margoengine/react, @margoengine/ui, margoengine | React component bindings for the stage |
| `react-dom` | 19.3.0 | MIT | optional peer | @margoengine/react, margoengine | React DOM root and portal rendering for scene and HTML components |
| `scheduler` | 0.28.0 | MIT | transitive (via react-dom) | margoengine | React DOM scheduling dependency |

None of them has an install script (`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`), a deprecation notice or a source other
than registry.npmjs.org with an integrity hash. Peers are installed by the app, not by us.

### Licence obligations and how they are met

- **Apache-2.0 (Draco, Basis, jxl-oxide under its Apache-2.0 option; Rapier as a peer).** Redistribution must carry the licence text, keep the upstream
  notices and mark modified files. `@margoengine/decoders` ships `dist/LICENSE-Apache-2.0.txt` and
  `dist/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md` (projects, sources, what changed); the modified `basis_transcoder.js` states the change
  in its first line. Neither upstream build ships a NOTICE file to carry forward. Rapier is not redistributed by us.
  The vendored files are byte-identical to the official releases (checked 2026-10-24; `.gitattributes` keeps them
  binary so checkouts do not change line endings):
  - Draco 1.5.6 glTF decoder from https://www.gstatic.com/draco/versioned/decoders/1.5.6/:

  - Draco 1.5.6 full decoder, for point clouds, from the same folder (checked 2026-11-06): `draco_decoder.wasm` (sha256
    `c55a594e8ffd18426d36b27fea9618af3df5e173640a3e56d46f09d76f0574f2`) and `draco_wasm_wrapper.js`
    (`e8049906ef3f8f75d3456c22a3f31bfdfe5b5b5bd09ccdec613b9e9a49d554d8`).
  - Basis Universal v1_50_0_2 WebGL transcoder from

    (`6cf17dc889352c42e9acf8897107978d127005fe3386c36a0e3845e27967630a`) and `basis_transcoder.js`
    (`8478b5b6d6b74e7d3082b89f6417321d8d1dc0307f2b30d4484bb11b441696a1`, before the build's static-embind step).
  - jxl-oxide-wasm 0.12.6 from npm, https://www.npmjs.com/package/jxl-oxide-wasm/v/0.12.6 (checked 2026-11-06):
    `jxl_oxide_wasm_bg.wasm` (sha256 `3336f3abd4a04fccc437e7a84f12d4b63c12f302044110867f99be14c4c75a69`) and

    `dist/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md`.

    https://github.com/BinomialLLC/basis_universal/tree/v1_50_0_2/webgl/encoder/build (checked 2026-11-06):
    `basis_encoder.wasm` (`dea2778b6d1705b4fdf12053e94cda0ac1cc4340a7e06911778a003ba785808a`) and

- **Optional local tool, never shipped (sharp and libvips).** sharp (Apache-2.0) and its prebuilt libvips binaries
  (LGPL-3.0) are installed as an optional dependency of Next.js for `examples/next`, and
  `scripts/optimize-demo-assets.js` and `scripts/build-scifi-helmet.mjs` use sharp to resize textures. `margo-convert
  build` also uses a sharp that is already installed in the project it runs in (WebP, AVIF and JPEG encoding, resizing);
  it is not a dependency or peer of any package, nothing is downloaded, and without it `margo-convert` falls back to
  its own PNG writer. Neither sharp nor libvips is in any tarball or served by the site.
- **MIT (React).** Keep the copyright and permission notice: npm dependencies carry their own
  LICENSE files.
- **Site and demos.** The site build copies this file to `/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, so the demos that bundle Draco,
  Basis or Rapier carry these notices next to the asset credits below.

## Development and workspace tooling (never shipped)

`package-lock.json` holds 188 third-party entries (build tools, test tools, the examples' and apps' own
dependencies, platform-optional binaries). Licences: MIT 95, Apache-2.0 46, MPL-2.0 12, LGPL-3.0-or-later 10, MIT OR Apache-2.0 9, ISC 4, Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later 3, BSD-3-Clause 3, BSD-2-Clause 2, 0BSD 1, Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT 1, CC-BY-4.0 1, MIT-0 1.
Install scripts anywhere in the lock: fsevents@2.3.3, webgpu@0.6.2. Deprecated: whatwg-encoding@3.1.1. `webgpu` is a development dependency only, for the Node proof of `@margoengine/headless`, and is never shipped; its
install script only clears the macOS quarantine flag on its binary. `rhino3dm` and `laz-perf` are not in the lock: the opt-in
`test:real-files:runtimes` tool of `@margoengine/loaders` fetches them at pinned versions into an ignored folder, for real-file tests only. CI and releases install with `npm ci`, which refuses a lockfile that does not match `package.json` and checks
every tarball against its integrity hash.
`aioquic` (BSD-3-Clause) is not in the lock: `packages/netcode/tests/webtransport-proof/server.py` uses it through a Python virtual environment of your own, for the by-hand WebTransport proof only. It is never shipped.

## Standard Utah Teapot control data

The numeric control net in packages/geometry/src/teapot-data.ts and the unchanged data fixture packages/geometry/tests/fixtures/teapotCGA.bpt represent the historic Utah Teapot developed at the University of Utah: Martin Newell (1975), Jim Blinn's proportions (1976), and Frank Crow's round bottom (1987). Model data only, under the standard-model exception in AGENTS.md; the Margo tessellator is clean-room code.
Source: Ryan Holmes's data-only mirror, http://www.holmes3d.net/graphics/teapot/teapotCGA.bpt , retrieved 2026-11-10; SHA-256 83c3cf09ff33cff17b8de714836c4c6758fccfc4288cef8671bacf0b7c294953. The University of Utah's model terms at https://graphics.cs.utah.edu/teapot/ permit any use, including commercial use, and request acknowledgement of the historic Utah Teapot and its University of Utah origin. The model is supplied without warranty. No third-party program or engine source is included.

Retained samples at strides 4,4,4; four modalities interleaved into little-endian float32, labels into uint8, both gzip-compressed. No interpolation/intensity scaling. Source/output hashes and affine are in msd-brain.json. These derived files retain CC BY-SA 4.0, are demo-only and are not distributed in engine packages. Independently authored engine implementation has no data-derived code. The adjacent demo also reuses existing CC0 OpenNeuro head.nrrd without modifying its source bytes.

### EMD-8117 demonstration density
examples/assets/sciviz/emdb-8117.bin contains retained original density samples at stride 3 from EMD-8117, TRPV1 with DkTx/RTX in a lipid nanodisc (2016). EMDB density data are CC0: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/about/public-data-access-statement. Source: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/emdb/structures/EMD-8117/map/emd_8117.map.gz. Full source/output hashes and reduction are recorded in emdb-8117.json; scripts/prepare-sciviz-emdb.mjs reproduces it. No source code or other-repository files were used in the engine implementation.



## Batch 241 standard voxel artwork and codec test data
packages/voxel-edit/tests/fixtures/formats-extra/arm.kv6 is Models/Player/Arm.kv6 from DeathByDenim, *OpenSpades Free assets* (2022), CC0 1.0: https://opengameart.org/content/openspades-free-assets-0 ; downloaded archive https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/models_6.zip ; licence https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ . arm.cub is a data-only conversion by the official vengi 0.6.0 executable, and arm.vmax is an original spec-encoded derivative retaining the downloaded model's surface geometry/colours. Attribution is retained although CC0 does not require it. These are standard test assets under AGENTS.md, not copied importer code. Other format fixtures and codec input data are original Margo test data. LZFSE compressed fixtures were generated by the public API of the prebuilt lzfse 0.4.2.post1 Python wheel (PyPI, BSD-3-Clause bindings and Apple's BSD-3-Clause codec); no oracle source, library, binary or runtime dependency is included, only compressed original test data.

## NASA TMR structured dataset fixtures
examples/assets/sciviz/datasets contains NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource flat-plate verification 35 by 25 PLOT3D grids, US government public domain. Source: https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/flatplate_grids.html ; original archive: https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/flatplategrids-grids.zip . The original PLOT3D bytes are unchanged. VTR, VTS and VTM are generated using VTK 9.7.2 public writer APIs from those measurements. VTR projects onto original coordinate lines, changing at most 2.0000112677109882e-12 units; VTS retains exact source coordinates. Source metadata and per-file SHA-256 digests are in source.json beside the data. packages/sciviz/tests/fixtures/datasets/vtk-oracle.json contains original outputs of VTK 9.7.2 public interpolation APIs on analytic reference cells, generated by packages/sciviz/scripts/datasets-fixtures.py. No VTK source or repository file was copied; these are tool-produced interoperability records. VTK runtime is an external test-generation tool under BSD-3-Clause, https://vtk.org/about/#license .
## Batch 175 public cloud-volume samples

`packages/sciviz/tests/fixtures/cloud-volumes/` contains small original metadata/object/Range snapshots, never full datasets, under the standard-sample-data exception. Each manifest records the original source, selected resolution and ROI, exact SHA-256 object bytes and independent-reference result. Original object bytes are kept unchanged, including their compression.

- `idr-lightsheet`: Florian F. Voigt et al., The mesoSPIM initiative (2019), IDR idr0066 experiment A, ExpA_VIP_ASLM_on. CC BY 4.0, University of Dundee/Voigt et al. Study and licence: https://idr.openmicroscopy.org/study/idr0066/ ; original OME-Zarr store: https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0066/ExpA_VIP_ASLM_on.zarr .
- `openorganelle`: Janelia COSEM/OpenOrganelle, jrc_hela-2 FIB-SEM uint16 image pyramid, Heinrich et al. CC BY 4.0. Source: https://openorganelle.janelia.org/ ; original N5: https://janelia-cosem-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/jrc_hela-2/jrc_hela-2.n5/em/fibsem-uint16 .
- `hemibrain`: Janelia FlyEM, Scheffer et al., hemibrain EM grayscale imagery. CC BY 4.0. Dataset and licence: https://www.janelia.org/project-team/flyem/hemibrain ; original precomputed source: https://storage.googleapis.com/neuroglancer-janelia-flyem-hemibrain/emdata/clahe_yz/jpeg .

Float32 ROI/reference files are numerical crops decoded from these sources, retaining their attribution. `fixtures/cloud-codecs` contains original analytic Margo samples compressed using binary numcodecs/LZ4/xxHash tools, not copied implementation or third-party dataset files. The Python generators name the tools and original sample formula. No third-party executable or library is shipped by this change.

Batch 188 environment/exr-codecs uses the AGENTS.md standard prebuilt decoder exception: unchanged OpenEXR 3.5.2 Wasm and compiled glue from EXRView 0.2.1, Sergen Eren (2026), MIT. Download https://sergeneren.gallery.vsassets.io/_apis/public/gallery/publisher/sergeneren/extension/exrview/0.2.1/assetbyname/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.VSIXPackage . Pinned hashes: packages/environment/vendor/exr-codecs/provenance.json. OpenEXR, Imath, OpenJPH, libdeflate and Zstandard notices are retained verbatim in that directory's ThirdPartyNotices.txt, and both licence files ship in dist/vendor/exr-codecs. The build emits an ESM export adapter and Node CJS copy of the glue; the original compiled source files remain unchanged. No viewer application or codec algorithm source is incorporated. The codecs/venice fixtures are CC0 derivatives of Greg Zaal / Poly Haven's Venice Sunset, with source and transforms in packages/environment/tests/fixtures/NOTICE.md.

Batch 188: packages/environment/tests/fixtures/venice_sunset_1k.hdr is Greg Zaal / Poly Haven's Venice Sunset photograph, CC0 1.0. Source https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/1k/venice_sunset_1k.hdr ; licence https://polyhaven.com/license ; SHA-256 and provenance in fixtures/NOTICE.md. Test data only, excluded from package tarballs.

Batch 180 geo-lod data: examples/assets/sciviz/geo-lod contains 21 unchanged Mapzen/AWS Terrarium PNGs, accessed 2026-11-10, https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/. Exact URLs, bytes and SHA-256 in source.json. These are standard geodata under the standard-asset exception, not external implementation files. Regional licences and mandatory credits are retained in attribution.txt with https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md; includes US public-domain SRTM/GMTED2010/3DEP/ETOPO1, CC BY and national open-data licences. The demo shows the complete provider credit beside the map.
